boundaries.note: Bottom two of the Superliga's qualifying playoff are relegated; top two of the 1. Division's promotion group are promoted. Both direct, no play-off.
Bottom two of the 1. Division's relegation group go down; top two of the 2. Division's promotion group go up. Direct.
Bottom two of the 2. Division's relegation group go down; top two of the 3. Division's promotion group go up. Direct.

conflicts.topic: Every level is a split competition
conflicts.detail: All four divisions are 12 clubs, 22 rounds, then a top-six promotion/championship group and a bottom-six relegation group of 10 more rounds (32 in total), with points carried. None of them is a plain double round-robin; a 'single, rounds: 22' model produces half a season.

conflicts.topic: The 3. Division relegates four, not two
conflicts.detail: The fourth tier's relegation group has six clubs and the bottom four go down to the Denmark Series; only two survive. That is a much steeper cut than at levels 1-3, where two go down.

conflicts.topic: No relegation play-off in the Superliga any more
conflicts.detail: The 2016-17 to 2018-19 format had a multi-step relegation play-off involving 1. Division clubs. Since the 12-club format (2019-20 onward) the bottom two of the qualifying playoff are relegated directly, which is what the 2025-26 relegation list (Fredericia 11th, Vejle 12th) shows.

conflicts.topic: Our ids name only one group of a split
conflicts.detail: DK3O ('2.Division') and DK4L ('3.Division') are the third and fourth tiers, not groups; the id suffixes look like geography but Denmark is a single national division at every modelled level.

notes: Season 2026-27 in progress. Sizes 12/12/12/12 and levels match our rows. Promotion/relegation at every boundary is 2 up / 2 down, direct, decided after the split. The 3. Division (DK4L) sends four down to the Denmark Series (level 5, not modelled). Reserve teams are not in the three national divisions (they play in the reserve league). Cups and UEFA competitions excluded.
